correctness.rationale: Character orthogonality yields exact pair-sum convolution (1). Hensel uniqueness for distinct nonopposite residues, cyclic convolution inside each residue class and the common zero fiber for antipodal classes prove exact identity (2) without omissions. Parseval and Cauchy--Schwarz give the explicit positive deficit and sharp constant 3p/2; their equality cases force one balanced opposite pair and one shared additive character. Signed residue representatives are distinguished from the code's shifted positive representatives. Standalone direct pair-sum and residue-block computations agree at p=3,5,7 for 15 exact decomposition comparisons plus 12 equality-packet checks; a separate direct Fourier average at p=3,5 confirms normalization. The all-odd-prime conclusion is analytic.

value.rationale: The unweighted modular hyperbola is a natural Kloosterman restriction surface; the sharp weighted quartic norm is its central finite-dimensional extension invariant. Over the first nilpotent modulus, the field-like flat optimizers disappear and rigid antipodal residue packets replace them. A complete all-odd-prime optimizer classification and a nonnegative global mass defect explain the transition and support future near-extremizer analysis. This is neither an arbitrary finite cutoff nor a known-table recomputation; the theorem solves a natural infinite family and exactly records its limitations.
